subject: Region-only model override request — Nebula Health (data residency)
messages:
From: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@nebulahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: region-only model + no-fallback for PHI flows

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. Nebula is finalizing procurement and a couple of infosec items came up in the last review: we need to ensure that for a subset of calls (PHI ingestion and patient-identifiable outputs) requests are pinned to a single US region and use a specific model family. Two hard asks from their compliance: 

- No automatic fallback to models outside the pinned region (no-fallback).
- Forced selection of the 7B quantized model variant (they validated for PII minimization).

They understand this is atypical but asked if Redwood can support a contractual exception or an operational configuration to guarantee these constraints for the production integration. They've attached a short MRP and a data map.

Can we schedule a quick ops/product sync to confirm feasibility and the risks/SLAs? Procurement is on the thread (procurement@nebulahealth.com).

Best,
Alex
Alex Gupta
Head of Platform Integrations
Nebula Health

Attachments: nebula_requirements_v1.pdf (pdf), nebula_data_map.csv (csv)

Thanks Alex — looping in product (Karthik), compliance (Hannah) and account lead (Lauren).

Quick summary of ask: Nebula wants a config that pins calls to a single US region and forces a named model variant; they also require an explicit no-fallback policy to prevent automatic routing to other model variants or regions. They want this in place for their PHI pipeline before the contract is signed.

Karthik — can you outline what is feasible today (hosted + dedicated) and what would require an exception or private deployment? Please call out operational trade-offs (outage modes, SLOs, and rollback paths).

Hannah — from compliance perspective, if we were to grant a no-fallback region lock, what additional evidence or controls would you need (audit logs, KMS/HSM, retention windows)?

Lauren — I expect some negotiation on price/SLA. If product flags this as requiring a Dedicated or Private deployment, we should surface that in the mutual action plan.

I can host a 30min sync this afternoon if that helps.

—Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-10T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: region-only model + no-fallback for PHI flows

Thanks — quick technical readout from product/infra perspective: 

Short answer: we can support region-locking and model pinning, but "no-fallback" as an absolute guarantee carries operational risk and will need explicit trade-offs in contract/operational runbooks. Details: 

1) Hosted API (standard tenant)
- Region hints + model selection are supported at the request layer.
- We do not currently provide a guarantee to refuse all cross-region fallbacks; the runtime will route to compatible resources if capacity in the pinned zone is exhausted.
- For strict no-fallback behavior we'd need an account-level routing policy that rejects requests when local capacity or model variant is unavailable. That is implementable as a configuration flag but is not in the standard SLA.

2) Dedicated / Reserved Capacity
- If Nebula buys Dedicated capacity in the specific region they can achieve practical no-fallback behavior provided we reserve sufficient headroom. This is the recommended path for predictability.
- Still: hardware failures or infra incidents could force a manual failover; if the customer demands automated refusal rather than fallback, we must accept that availability could drop to 0 during incidents.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Gives the strongest guarantee for both data residency and strict model variant control.
- Requires longer lead time and an enterprise procurement loop.

Operational caveats and asks
- SLO waiver: product requests that Nebula accept a reduced availability SLA for the pinned flow if they insist on absolute no-fallback.
- Monitoring / runbooks: we must add specific alerts and an ops playbook to handle reject conditions (traffic rejection, queued retries).
- Auditability: we should record a token-level routing decision and include it in retention exports for compliance.

Suggested next steps
- Marissa / Lauren: confirm whether they are open to Dedicated or Private options as part of the deal economics.
- Hannah: list the exact audit/retention/KMS artifacts Nebula needs (I can add product-level support once we have that).
- Follow-up: 30–45min with Nebula to walk through trade-offs and draft the runbook language we would include in the security appendix.

If useful I can also enumerate the code-level knobs to flip (routing policy: reject_on_unavailable=true, model_pin=redwood-7b-q) for an internal RFC.

—Karthik

Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-12T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: region-only model + no-fallback for PHI flows

Thanks all — compliance quick notes based on the MRP: 

- Audit logs: we need per-request routing/decision logs retained for 5 years for regulated flows. Log format should include routing_decision, model_pin, region, request_id, and timestamp.
- Key management: Nebula requires customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for model artifacts and token metadata. We need to confirm KMS integration in the chosen deployment mode.
- Data handling: confirm that model cache and KV stores are collocated with the region and have defined TTLs; Nebula's data map shows several long-lived caches that we must address.

If we move forward with a contractual no-fallback (i.e., runtime rejects requests on capacity shortage), compliance will require: 
1) Explicit acceptance of availability risk by Nebula in contract language.
2) Access to routing/audit logs for quarterly audits.
3) A playbook for incident response that includes notification timelines for both parties.

Lauren — Marissa flagged commercial implications. If Nebula is willing to sign up for Dedicated reserved capacity (with a headroom buffer), compliance is comfortable with that approach, provided the KMS and log retention items are satisfied.

Happy to join the customer call to walk through the compliance appendix.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
